positions.name: DeriveIdE2eTestScope
positions.frame: what must the derive-id end-to-end test reproduce from production, and what must it guarantee holds despite that failure pattern?
positions.why: src-1 names the exact production failure condition the test is built to reproduce (missing-id, ## heading); src-2 states the invariant the test must enforce in that condition (no crash, valid slug). Read together they define one test's complete scope — the trigger and the guarantee — rather than two independent facts. There is a mild tension in register: src-1 reads as a plain diagnostic claim (what the test does) while src-2 reads as a settled operational must-rule (what it is required to guarantee); the frame holds both as facets of the same test's design rather than resolving one into the other.
positions.why_no_under: no strata or structure node in scope names test infrastructure or e2e testing; the only supplied strata item (ns__Decision_DiagnosticFirst under ns__Strategy) concerns consulting methodology, not this test's subject matter.

placements.why: This envelope's content (a test that deliberately reproduces a documented production failure pattern and asserts a hard invariant about its outcome) is organizational-strategy grain about how the org substantiates correctness claims — proof-by-reproduction rather than description. No strata category exists yet in this repo ('none yet'), and nothing in the supplied ns__Decision_DiagnosticFirst / ns__Strategy material (consulting methodology) is close enough to be an EXACT or INSPIRED fit for a validation/proof category. This is the NEW case: mint exactly the one strata node this content calls for, standalone, with no forced parent.

placements.frame: Does this expression test, guarantee, or newly evidence that id/slug derivation from headings survives a malformed, missing-id, or production-observed edge case without crashing while still emitting a valid slug?
placements.why: src-1 names the exact production failure condition being reproduced (## heading, no id field) and src-2 states the invariant the derivation logic must hold under it (no crash, valid slug) — together, per the position pass's DeriveIdE2eTestScope reading, these define one recurring subject: derive-id/slug robustness against malformed heading input. This passes the narrative grain test — it is a theme future test envelopes (more malformed-input cases, more production failure patterns) will keep feeding, not a one-time fact — so it earns its own leaf rather than joining an existing one, since no existing leaf or strata category (both empty in this repo) covers it.
